name: François Chollet
category: Deep learning library creator / AI researcher (Keras)
milestone_by_age_26: Created and released Keras, a widely adopted high-level deep learning library for Python, around February–March 2015 at age 25; joined Google shortly after.
early_history_summary: French engineer born 20 October 1989; earned a Diplôme d'Ingénieur (MEng) from ENSTA Paris (Polytechnic Institute of Paris) in 2012. Built Keras as a side project in early 2015 during the pre-framework-standardization wave of deep learning, then joined Google where Keras became tightly integrated with TensorFlow.
primary_early_advantage_tags: ENSTA Paris, deep learning wave 2015, open-source Keras, Google integration
evidence_summary: Chollet released Keras at 25 in the 2015 deep-learning boom, then joined Google where it became a default high-level API path into TensorFlow. Elite French engineering education plus open-source distribution and structural ML wave are the clearest advantages; family background is not documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born 20 October 1989 in France; trained as an engineer at ENSTA Paris (MEng 2012).
current_position: AI researcher and entrepreneur after leaving Google (2024); co-founded AGI-focused lab with Zapier co-founder Mike Knoop; creator of Keras and ARC-AGI / ARC Prize.

trajectory.event: Graduated ENSTA Paris with a Diplôme d'Ingénieur (MEng).
Released Keras deep learning library and joined Google shortly afterward.
Published Xception paper and Deep Learning with Python book, amplifying Keras adoption.
Published ARC-AGI benchmark paper On the Measure of Intelligence.
Named to TIME100 AI; left Google after 9+ years; launched ARC Prize competition.
Co-founded new AGI/program-synthesis lab and expanded ARC Prize into a foundation.

name: Amjad Masad
milestone_by_age_26: Replit co-founded in 2016 when he was about age 28 (sources place birth ~1987–1988; US move ~2011–2012 at age 23–24). Codecademy founding-engineer role (2011–2013) was employment, not an independently documented personal product/founder breakout by 26.
family_context_summary: Born and raised in Amman, Jordan, modest family with Palestinian heritage; father a civil engineer.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a civil engineer who emphasized education.
evidence_summary: Replit co-founded in 2016 when he was about age 28; prior Codecademy founding-engineer and Facebook JS infrastructure roles were employment. No clear independently verified personal product/founder milestone by age 26 in reviewed sources.

name: Wes Bos
milestone_by_age_26: Major educational breakout (JavaScript30, React for Beginners, Syntax podcast, large course business) arrived mid/late 2010s when he was ~28–30+; early freelance consulting (BosType from ~2005) is real but not a clearly material public milestone comparable to product/framework fame by age 26.
evidence_summary: Self-reports ~38 years old with ~26 years making websites and long-running freelance practice from Hamilton, Ontario, but the material educator brand (JS30 and major paid courses) is post-26. No independently dated breakout product/award by age 26 found.

name: Addy Osmani
category: Browser engineer / Chrome developer experience leader
milestone_by_age_26: At age 16 (2002–2003), built XWebs, an ambitious C++ web browser with multi-connection download optimizations; entered Esat BT Young Scientist of the Year and received Wired and Irish Examiner coverage in January 2003.
early_history_summary: Born March 1986 in Ireland; as a sixth-year student at St. Finian's College in Mullingar he spent ~2 years coding XWebs (hundreds of thousands of lines of C++), demonstrating early systems/web-performance obsession. Later became a long-tenured Google Chrome engineering leader (DevTools, Lighthouse, Core Web Vitals) and Cloud AI developer-experience director.
family_context_summary: Raised in Mullingar, Ireland; detailed parental professions/wealth not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: teen browser builder, Young Scientist competition, Wired coverage, later Chrome DX
evidence_summary: Osmani's by-26 milestone is the documented teenage XWebs browser project with national competition and Wired coverage at ~16. Later Chrome/Google leadership compounded technical depth and platform wave rather than inherited capital. Family background remains sparsely documented.
starting_point: Born March 1986 in Ireland; secondary school at St. Finian's College, Mullingar, where he built a full browser as a teen science project.
current_position: Engineering and AI developer-experience leader after ~14 years at Google (Chrome DX, then Google Cloud AI); author and open-source contributor focused on AI-assisted engineering.

trajectory.event: Debuted XWebs browser at Esat BT Young Scientist competition; covered by Wired.
Joined Google Chrome engineering, beginning long DevTools/developer-experience tenure.
Became a central figure in Chrome DevTools and front-end performance tooling.
Helped shape Lighthouse and Core Web Vitals era of web performance standards.
Moved into Google Cloud AI developer experience / agent tooling leadership, then transitioned toward independent writing and projects.

name: ThePrimeagen (Michael B. Paulson)
milestone_by_age_26: Public fame as ThePrimeagen (Twitch/YouTube programming educator) and high-visibility Netflix engineering storytelling arrived well after age 26; by-26 record is ordinary employment path without a dated personal product/framework/company breakout in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Michael Paulson worked ~10 years at Netflix then built a large streaming/education brand; no material independently dated founder/OSS breakout by age 26 found in reviewed sources.

name: Theo Browne
category: Developer tools founder / web developer educator (t3.gg, Ping)
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Ping Labs (YC W22, Winter 2022) and popularized the T3 Stack / create-t3-app ecosystem around ages 24–25 after Twitch engineering and a fast-growing YouTube channel.
early_history_summary: RPI alumnus and former Twitch software engineer who shifted into full-time content and founder mode. Built audience around modern TypeScript/Next.js practices, then founded Ping (W22) and catalyzed create-t3-app as a community scaffolding project for the T3 Stack.
primary_early_advantage_tags: YouTube audience, Twitch eng, YC W22, T3 Stack, TypeScript/Next wave
evidence_summary: Theo's by-26 milestone is founder entry via YC W22 Ping Labs plus T3 Stack / create-t3-app influence while still mid-20s. Distribution from content and structural TypeScript/Next.js wave matter more than documented family capital. Exact birth day is less documented than cohort year ~1997 from candidate metadata and career timing.
starting_point: US path through RPI and Twitch engineering into content creation and YC founding (family background not documented).
current_position: CEO/founder around T3 Chat and related products (Ping/UploadThing ecosystem); major web-dev YouTuber and investor-operator.

trajectory.event: Joined Twitch as a software engineer, gaining large-scale web systems experience.
Grew t3.gg YouTube/education brand while building modern TypeScript full-stack projects.
Founded Ping Labs in YC W22 and popularized the T3 Stack / create-t3-app scaffolding path.
Scaled UploadThing and related developer tools alongside content business.
Expanded into T3 Chat / AI products with multi-million ARR creator-founder economics reported publicly.

name: Gergely Orosz
milestone_by_age_26: The Pragmatic Engineer newsletter/brand and major public influence arrived after big-tech roles (Skype/Uber etc.) well after age 26; no material independently dated founder/OSS/product breakout by 26 found in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Career path through engineering roles then independent publishing; public breakout as Pragmatic Engineer is post-26. No by-26 material personal milestone documented in reviewed sources.

name: Kent C. Dodds
milestone_by_age_26: Born 1988; BYU MS Information Systems 2014 (~age 26) then industry/education rise. React Testing Library and full-time educator fame (egghead, Epic React) are mid/late 2010s at ~29–31+, not a by-26 material product breakout.
family_context_summary: Born Twin Falls, Idaho; large family of 12 children; LDS mission then BYU.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as software-domain advantage in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Kent's own about page places birth in 1988 and BYU graduation in 2014; Testing Library / educator dominance is after age 26. No material dated OSS/product milestone by 26 found.

name: Sarah Drasner
category: Front-end engineer / Vue core / engineering leader
milestone_by_age_26: Vue core team membership, major conference circuit, Microsoft/Google engineering leadership, and SVG/animation book fame are mid-career after age 26; no clear independently dated material product/founder breakout by age 26 found in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Recognized Vue/CSS/engineering-leadership career is well documented post-26; reviewed sources do not establish a specific material milestone at or before age 26.

name: Simon Willison
milestone_by_age_26: Co-created the Django web framework while on industrial placement at the Lawrence Journal-World (2003–2004) and saw it open-sourced publicly in July 2005 at age 24.
early_history_summary: British programmer born January 1981; early professional web work from ~2000, University of Bath CS, influential PHP XML-RPC library and early blog/pingback work. Co-built Django with Holovaty, Kaplan-Moss, and Miner at a newspaper during placement year, then graduated 2005 and continued high-impact open-source and product work (Lanyrd, Datasette, AI tooling commentary).
primary_early_advantage_tags: Lawrence Journal-World placement, Django cofounders, Python web wave, early blogging
evidence_summary: Willison's material by-26 milestone is co-creating Django and its 2005 public open-source release at 24. Complementary cofounder team, newspaper product pressure, and the mid-2000s Python web framework wave are well documented; family capital is not.
starting_point: Born January 1981 in the UK; early webmaster work then University of Bath Computer Science.
current_position: Independent open-source developer and writer; creator of Datasette; PSF board member; influential voice on LLMs, prompt injection, and agentic engineering.

trajectory.event: Professional web development at Gameplay (UK) as webmaster/developer.
Began industrial placement at Lawrence Journal-World where Django was created with teammates.
Django open-sourced publicly; graduated University of Bath.
Co-founded Lanyrd with Natalie Downe (later YC-funded, Eventbrite acquisition).
Released Datasette, becoming a defining tool for publishing SQLite-backed data.
Coined and popularized the term prompt injection in LLM security discourse.

name: Shawn Wang (swyx)
milestone_by_age_26: Left quant finance and taught himself to code mid-career (~2017 bootcamp era at about age 29); learn-in-public, Netlify/AWS/Temporal DX leadership, and 'Rise of the AI Engineer' fame are post-26.
family_context_summary: Grew up in Singapore; later US/UK career. Detailed family finances not documented.
evidence_summary: Public narrative is finance-to-code career switch after age 26; AI Engineer Summit / Latent Space influence is 2020s. No by-26 software breakout documented.

name: Charity Majors
milestone_by_age_26: Honeycomb co-founded in 2016 (~age 33). Earlier Linden Lab / Parse / Facebook ops leadership was employment; no material independently dated founder/product breakout by age 26 found in reviewed sources (on-call-from-17 anecdotes are not a public milestone).
family_context_summary: Described in some profiles as homeschooled outsider path; detailed family wealth not documented.
evidence_summary: Honeycomb founding (2016 with Christine Yen) is the clear material founder milestone and is post-26. Prior Parse/Facebook systems work does not meet personal by-26 product/founder bar under strict rubric.
